# wso2is_inbound_provisioning_configuration (Resource)

Manages inbound SCIM provisioning for requests that sign in with basic authentication (the resident service provider). Requests that use an application's OAuth2 token follow that application's own provisioning settings instead. The resource only changes the settings that you set. Other settings keep their current values. When you destroy this resource, the provider restores the server defaults. Each tenant (or organization) has one set of these settings. To import them, use the ID `inbound_provisioning_configuration`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Send every user created through /scim2 with basic authentication to one user store.
# While this is set, the server ignores the DOMAIN/ prefix of new users (including
# wso2is_user.user_store) and rejects SCIM updates of users in other user stores.
# Destroying the resource clears it.
resource "wso2is_inbound_provisioning_configuration" "this" {
  provisioning_userstore = "CUSTOMERS"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `provisioning_userstore` (String) The user store that receives every user created through `/scim2`. The default, `""`, lets the `DOMAIN/` prefix of each username choose the user store. **When you set a user store, the server ignores the user store of new users, including `wso2is_user.user_store`. It also refuses SCIM updates of users in other user stores.**
- `proxy_mode` (Boolean) Forward SCIM provisioning requests to outbound connectors without storing users locally.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Always `inbound_provisioning_configuration`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import wso2is_inbound_provisioning_configuration.this inbound_provisioning_configuration
```
